subject: Concealing cables and equipment
hook: Behind closed doors or on an open shelf: where should the soundbar and set-top box live?
ig:
Behind closed doors or on an open shelf: where should the soundbar and set-top box live?

It is one of the first choices on any media wall, and it is not just about looks.

A: Behind closed doors
The calmest option. No boxes, no blinking lights. The trade-off: equipment gets warm, so it needs ventilation, and solid doors can block remote controls and weaken Wi-Fi from a router.

B: On an open shelf
Air moves freely, remotes work and everything is easy to reach. The trade-off: every box and cable connection stays visible, so the shelf needs keeping tidy.

A lot of people end up in the middle: closed cupboards for consoles and storage, with one open shelf or a slatted front for anything that needs a line of sight.

Which are you, A or B? And which device in your living room causes the most trouble? Let us know in the comments.
fb:
Quick Sunday question for anyone planning a TV unit or media wall: would you hide your equipment behind doors, or keep it on an open shelf?

Doors look calmer, but kit gets warm and some remotes will not work through a solid front. Open shelves are practical, but you see every box and light. Plenty of people split the difference with one open shelf, or slatted doors that let air and signal through.
